subject: tools/m1_boot_install.py J293 stage2 boot.bin install/restore (delta bound to window candidate attempt 4)

candidate_binding.PREFIX_BYTES: 0x420000, shared by the footprint check and slice; matches receipt candidate_payload_offset 4325376 and m1n1-window.bin size
candidate_binding.receipt: reports/sprint-008/window-candidate-build.json attempt 4; the reviewer recomputed the proposed-boot.bin and m1n1-window.bin hashes, which match.
candidate_binding.original_tag_check_by_reviewer: The bound original image contains exactly one ##m1n1_ver##f5a82fdb-dirty tag in its first 0x400000 bytes, matching the stage2 version the tool accepts and root's live /chosen readback.

confirmed: Everything confirmed in revision 1 still holds: plan by default, exact-byte gating with the byte-identical Linux suffix (consistent with m1n1 _payload_start = _end), CAS before plan, backup and rename, dedicated O_EXCL backup, boot.bin.old untouched, one-shot private intent, staged O_EXCL temp, os.replace, directory fsync, and no reboot, NVRAM, stage1, partition or boot-policy writes.

G2 is implemented: findmnt PARTUUID of the /boot/efi mount must equal /chosen asahi,efi-system-partition, and /chosen asahi,m1n1-stage2-version must be f5a82fdb-dirty (the original's embedded tag) or the reviewed candidate tag. A missing property fails closed.

C2 is implemented: verify_after_sync runs fsync, then POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED, then re-hash for both the backup and the replaced target, so file data is re-read from storage. The comment correctly says this is not a power-loss durability test.
C3 is implemented: any leftover .boot.bin.darwin-lab-*.tmp or any operation intent without result.json blocks new plans, including restore, pending manual review.
C1 is mostly implemented: a post-write storage mismatch raises BOOT_FILE_UNVERIFIED_DO_NOT_REBOOT, writes no result.json, and keeps the incomplete intent and the verified backup for manual review.

recommended_before_install.resolution: BootFileUnverified wraps the directory fsync, storage re-read and result.json sequence after os.replace, and main() emits BOOT_FILE_UNVERIFIED_DO_NOT_REBOOT for it. A failure after a verified replace (e.g. result.json) is also reported as do-not-reboot, which is conservative.
recommended_before_install.residual: os.replace itself is just outside the typed block. An exception raised by the rename (possible mid-operation on vfat) reports the generic REFUSED status although boot.bin state is uncertain. Moving os.replace inside the try would close it; until then the controller should treat any execute-mode failure as do-not-reboot.
recommended_before_install.issue: main() prints the generic status REFUSED_OR_INCOMPLETE_NO_BOOT_VERDICT for every exception, including BOOT_FILE_UNVERIFIED_DO_NOT_REBOOT after os.replace and any failure after a successful replace (e.g. writing result.json). A caller keyed on status could read that as 'nothing changed' and reboot.
recommended_before_install.fix: Track the execute phase. When any ESP write has happened, emit a distinct status (e.g. BOOT_STORAGE_CHANGED_UNVERIFIED_DO_NOT_REBOOT) plus boot_file_replaced true/false, and make the M5 controller refuse resets on anything except BOOT_FILE_REPLACED_NOT_BOOT_VALIDATED or a plan-only/no-change result.

remaining_gates.gate: No non-persistent candidate launch exists in the original stage2, so the first persistent candidate boot needs one-time owner availability and a prepared manual Recovery rollback (copy the verified ESP backup over m1n1/boot.bin; boot picker as last resort). The tool's restore requires a running Linux and cannot help if the candidate stops before Linux.
Hold the M5 per-target lock and pause unattended resets for the whole install. Linux vfat rename over an existing file is not crash-atomic; the tool does not itself coordinate with the controller.

minor_notes: Mount parsing still requires exactly one /proc/mounts row at /boot/efi (fails closed on autofs stacking); validate_machine is still patched out in tests, while the pure identity check now has a test.
An intent left by an early refusal (e.g. CAS drift before backup) also blocks later operations until a human removes it, which is conservative and should be documented.
The original slice offset 0x400000 is a literal; naming it beside ORIGINAL_SHA would make the binding clearer.
limits: Source review only; the reviewer did not run the 17 host tests.
Linux vfat fsync/rename and FADV_DONTNEED behavior are reasoned from general kernel behavior; FAT metadata buffers are not dropped by the re-read.
A replaced boot file is not a boot test.
